title: Subsheaves of a constructible sheaf on a Noetherian scheme
statement:
Let $T$ be Noetherian and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring. Every
subsheaf of a constructible $\Lambda$-module sheaf on the small etale site
is constructible.

note:
*Source note:* this is Stacks Project, Section 59.74, Constructible sheaves
on Noetherian schemes ([Tag 03RY](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03RY)),
whose Proposition 59.74.1 (3) states that for a Noetherian scheme $X$ and a
Noetherian ring $\Lambda$ every submodule and quotient module of a
constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ is constructible (the
weak Serre input being Lemma 59.71.6, [Tag
03RZ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03RZ)). The blueprint's statement
is the same assertion for a finite commutative ring $\Lambda$, which is
Noetherian, on the small etale site of a Noetherian $T$, and it adds a
self-contained proof by Noetherian induction on geometric stalks in place of
Stacks' proof through a finite partition into locally constant pieces.

proof.text: Use isConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf_iff to convert the finite constant-value constructibility hypothesis on F to the existing IsConstructibleSheaf predicate.

A finite commutative ring is Noetherian (the Mathlib finite-module Noetherian instance). Apply constructible_of_mono_noetherian to the given monomorphism G -> F. Its generic-constancy and closed-subscheme Noetherian-induction proof gives IsConstructibleSheaf G.
Convert the conclusion back through isConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf_iff. The statement and all hypotheses are unchanged, including finiteness of the ring and Noetherianity of the scheme.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 59.74.1(3), Proposition 09BH(3), and the existing constructibility comparison; specialized to a finite coefficient ring by J1

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against Stacks Tags 03RY and 03RZ and found no sorry-free declaration stating arbitrary constructible subsheaf closure. Added one smaller unsplit lemma for generic constancy of a subsheaf of a constant finite sheaf, searched in Mathlib, and rewrote the three proof steps to cite the existing irreducible-lisse-strata, finite-components, flat-open, stalk-exactness and stalk-conservativity nodes. The final step spells out the Noetherian induction and gluing of the generic open with the inductive partition of its closed complement.
